Mitoses and Ki-67 staining of 20%-40% support active proliferation, not an independent low-grade subtype designation
decisive_items: Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells originated from one lateral end, pushing down into the dermis and involving many hairs
Malignant squamous cells contained eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli; mitotic figures were present
Classic-appearing hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
response.rationale: R2 is directly supported by raw histopathologic spans describing neoplastic squamous proliferation, dermal/hair involvement, and malignant squamous cells with mitoses. C1 retains the same SCC diagnosis but adds 'well-differentiated' as a subtype completion, which is not supported by any supplied raw span; that subtype claim rests on generator opinion rather than raw evidence. Therefore R2 is the safer raw-grounded champion, with C1 as a less well-supported refinement.
